key_insight: When an object is manipulated in front of fixed cameras, its motion creates effective new viewpoints in the object’s local frame; estimating those object-centric transforms lets a system synthesize these virtual views and recover much more detailed geometry and appearance than static multi-view setups permit.
problem_solved: Overcomes the severe viewpoint limitation of sparse, fixed-camera rigs by exploiting opportunistic object motion (e.g., human manipulation) to produce additional virtual viewpoints for high-quality 3D reconstruction.
method: Detect and track the object through time and estimate object-centric transforms induced by manipulation (aligning frames to an object coordinate frame).
Re-project and aggregate image evidence from many temporally-separated frames as virtual camera viewpoints around the object.
Jointly optimize geometry and appearance (e.g., multi-view stereo / neural rendering in object frame) to produce high-fidelity shape and texture from sparse physical cameras.
impact: Makes high-quality 3D capture feasible with inexpensive, static camera setups and natural human interaction—beneficial for AR/VR content creation, robotic perception, and scalable dataset collection without elaborate turntables or camera rigs.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: fixed cameras watching a moving object vs. equivalent virtual orbiting cameras in the object frame.
Pipeline flowchart: detection → object-centric alignment → virtual view aggregation → geometry & appearance optimization.
Before/after reconstructions: coarse result from static views only vs. detailed reconstruction using opportunistic motion.
Viewpoint coverage heatmap showing increased angular coverage achieved through object motion.
paper_title: Detailed Geometry and Appearance from Opportunistic Motion
paper_authors: Ryosuke Hirai, Kohei Yamashita, Antoine Guédon, Ryo Kawahara, Vincent Lepetit
